Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 mins
Location: Zoom
Record owner: fireflies.ai exporter
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Zhou (CTO - Arbor), Marco Ruiz (Head of IT - Arbor), Priya Nair (Compliance), Samir Patel (ML Engineer)

Summary (auto):
Arbor is evaluating a hermetic on-prem/private deployment of Redwood for clinical imaging assist. Major concerns: offline update process, hardware SKU compatibility, patch windows and air-gap logistics, key management/HSM, and auditability for regulatory audits. Next steps focused on hardware sizing, documentation handoff, and scheduling an on-site ops review.

Topics:
- Regulatory constraints and audit-readiness
- Offline/air-gapped update mechanics and allowed artifact transfer
- Hardware footprint and GPU lifecycle
- Networking constraints and remote support options
- Cost tradeoffs: Dedicated vs Private hermetic nodes

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh I'm Sofia from Redwood, account exec on this. We have Ethan from our solutions engineering team and then I think we have the Arbor crew, could we do quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Lena Zhou: yeah hi I'm Lena CTO at Arbor Neurotech, we build inference-assisted MRI post-processing pipelines, working in regulated clinics.
[00:21] Marco Ruiz: Marco here, head of IT, I manage the data center and the air-gapped nodes for regulatory workloads.
[00:27] Priya Nair: Priya, compliance; I handle HIPAA and internal audit prep.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Samir, ML eng, I care about model latency and the KV cache behavior across offline restarts.
[00:38] Ethan Cole: great, thanks, hi all. Quick agenda — understand your constraints, sketch deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private hermetic), deep dive on offline update workflow, hardware, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:47] Dr. Lena Zhou: yes that's perfect.
[00:50] Sofia Martinez: quick qualification — are you currently using any managed LLM endpoints or self-hosted inference today?
[00:57] Marco Ruiz: currently internal cluster, a mix of inference on-prem and some experimental cloud for non-PHI. For clinical workloads we keep it fully segregated, no egress.
[01:06] Priya Nair: and we have strict change control — updates go through security review, signoff, and are applied during quarterly maintenance windows.
[01:12] Ethan Cole: noted. What's the primary success criteria for a Redwood deployment? Is it throughput, latency, auditability, or cost?
[01:20] Dr. Lena Zhou: combination — latency needs to be under ~80ms p50 for the small models we use in prefetching, throughput for batch jobs is important overnight, and everything must have immutable audit logs for regulatory review.
[01:33] Samir Patel: also, we need the ability to pin exact model versions and roll back if a model regression occurs.
[01:40] Sofia Martinez: makes total sense. From a product standpoint we offer Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private hermetic. For your use-case the Private hermetic node (air-gapped) is what we usually recommend. Ethan, can you say a bit about how our private hermetic package addresses offline updates?
[01:54] Ethan Cole: sure. In hermetic mode we provide a signed artifact bundle — model weights, runtime images, and a signed manifest. Customers ingest bundles via approved USB or scp over an isolated transfer node depending on their policy. The node verifies signatures using customer-managed keys or Redwood-signed keys. There's support for HSM integration for key unwrap (we support several KMS/HSM flows).
[02:18] Marco Ruiz: when you say customer-managed keys, do you mean we can keep keys inside our HSM and Redwood never sees them?
[02:25] Ethan Cole: yes, you can keep master keys in your HSM; we support wrapping/unwrapping flows so only wrapped keys are exchanged. We can also integrate with on-prem KMS like HashiCorp Vault or AWS CloudHSM if you have those appliances.
[02:36] Priya Nair: for auditability, we need to ensure every update has a signed chain and we can show who triggered the change and when. Do you produce a tamper-evident audit log?
[02:45] Ethan Cole: yes, the hermetic node writes append-only audit logs to a local tamper-evident store and we provide a signed export package you can attach to audits. We also support a read-only export for auditors.
[02:55] Dr. Lena Zhou: on the hardware side, what GPUs and memory footprint are you recommending? Our racks are 1U and we have limited power headroom.
[03:04] Ethan Cole: we typically recommend A40 or H100-class depending on model precision and q8/q4 quantization. For smaller LLMs with quantization and continuous KV cache, you can get by with A40 or RTX 6000-class. For larger LLMs that you might want to run at higher throughput, H100 is better but higher power. We'll produce a footprint doc.
[03:20] Marco Ruiz: can you quantify — like how many tokens per second per GPU for the model sizes?
[03:25] Ethan Cole: rough numbers: a 7B quantized model on an A40 can do ~15-25 tokens/sec depending on batch; an H100 could do 40-80 tokens/sec. Those are ballpark; we'll run a benchmark on your workload.
[03:36] Samir Patel: benchmark is key — our token distribution is spiky, many short requests then occasional long batch jobs overnight.
[03:42] Sofia Martinez: got it. Let's talk about update cadence. You mentioned quarterly windows — do you require live rolling updates or full node restart?
[03:50] Marco Ruiz: we prefer full restarts during the maintenance window, patch windows are rigid. No network egress during update artifacts upload.
[03:57] Ethan Cole: that's fine. Our hermetic package supports both full image replacement and in-place runtime swap. For strict air-gapped workflows we recommend a full image replacement approach to ensure clean state. The process: deliver signed bundle -> staging node validation -> operator triggers install -> restart -> smoke tests.
[04:14] Priya Nair: who performs smoke tests? We need auditor-friendly verification steps.
[04:19] Ethan Cole: Redwood can provide an ops playbook with deterministic smoke tests you can run locally. We can also run a remote verification if you permit an allowlisted temporary connection, but we know that's rare.
[04:31] Dr. Lena Zhou: is there a small telemetry fingerprint you could provide that isn't PHI but lets you confirm successful deploy? We can't allow any PHI to leave the network.
[04:41] Ethan Cole: yes, we can provide a zero-PII deploy verification checksum and signature verification that you can send out-of-band, or you can return a signed success bundle for us to ingest manually.
[04:53] Sofia Martinez: quick question on backup and snapshotting — do hermetic nodes support snapshotting KV cache and rehydration across restarts?
[04:59] Ethan Cole: yes, local KV snapshotting is supported; snapshots are stored encrypted at rest and can be exported as encrypted artifacts for backup. Rehydration is a local operation.
[05:10] Marco Ruiz: patch management — how long does a typical image update take? We budget 2 hours per node during window.
[05:16] Ethan Cole: typical replacement + smoke tests for a single node is 20–45 minutes; full fleet depends on orchestration. If you do serial restarts one node at a time, it's linear. We'll map it against your fleet size.
[05:26] Priya Nair: for compliance, we also need SSO and RBAC integration — do you support SAML/SCIM?
[05:31] Ethan Cole: yes, hermetic control plane supports SAML and SCIM via an optional management appliance. For fully air-gapped customers we provide a control plane appliance that can run in your management VLAN and integrate with your IdP.
[05:43] Samir Patel: curious about model governance — can we pin model versions and apply A/B rules offline?
[05:49] Ethan Cole: yes, rollouts are config-driven. The hermetic nodes read a rollout manifest and can revert to pinned versions. A/B is more complicated offline, but you can run local routing rules to split traffic between versions as long as the routing manifest is in the artifact.
[06:03] Dr. Lena Zhou: question on support SLA — we are a clinical partner; we need 24-hour incident turnaround for Sev1 during clinic hours. How does that look for an air-gapped deployment?
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: for Private hermetic customers we offer an enterprise support tier with on-call SEs; we will sign an SLA, but remote troubleshooting is limited by connectivity. We do options: remote allowlist, or on-site support dispatch (via contract).
[06:23] Marco Ruiz: can you dispatch staff on site? We have to pre-clear contractors.
[06:28] Sofia Martinez: yes, we have authorized engineers for on-site engagements under our enterprise agreements; we'd need to coordinate security clearance and PO.
[06:34] Samir Patel: what about CPU fallback? If GPU fails, is there ability to degrade to CPU fallback to keep service up?
[06:40] Ethan Cole: possible but impractical for performance-critical inference. We can advise on multi-GPU redundancy and hot-swap approaches; CPU fallback would be extremely slow and only for emergency.
[06:50] Dr. Lena Zhou: data residency — we need all logs and model artifacts to remain on-prem. Confirm?
[06:55] Ethan Cole: confirmed — hermetic keeps all artifacts, logs, and telemetry local. Any export is explicitly triggered and signed.
[07:02] Marco Ruiz: about the signed manifest — what signature algorithm do you use? We run FIPS appliances.
[07:08] Ethan Cole: we support RSA and ECDSA and can sign using FIPS-compliant certs. If you use an HSM, we can perform verification via wrapped keys.
[07:17] Priya Nair: auditors will ask for chain-of-custody for model artifacts, can you provide metadata that ties a model to a release ticket?
[07:24] Ethan Cole: yes, the manifest contains release id, hash, build metadata, and optionally a CVE/binary bill of materials (SBOM) excerpt.
[07:33] Sofia Martinez: quick commercial question — are you evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity vs fully hermetic private?
[07:38] Dr. Lena Zhou: we looked at Redwood Dedicated but given our regulated workloads we think Private hermetic is necessary. Cost is a factor though — we need numbers to compare.
[07:47] Sofia Martinez: we'll share a pricing comparison matrix (Dedicated vs Private hermetic) and an opex/ capex breakdown.
[07:54] Samir Patel: one technical edge-case — if the KV cache gets corrupted during a shutdown, what's the recovery path?
[07:59] Ethan Cole: we have checksum-verified snapshots; on corruption we can revert to previous valid snapshot and replay logs if available. We'll include recovery steps in the ops playbook.
[08:10] Marco Ruiz: outage tolerance — what about multi-node consensus? Do you recommend active-active or active-standby?
[08:16] Ethan Cole: for hermetic on-prem we usually recommend active-standby with load balancer since cross-node synchronization without a central control plane in air-gapped mode is tricky. You can design active-active but it'll require more complex sync and you'll want to accept potential split-brain during some operations.
[08:30] Dr. Lena Zhou: what about hardware lifecycle — in three years do we need to re-quantize models? How disruptive are model format changes?
[08:38] Ethan Cole: our runtime supports multiple quantized formats; model upgrades sometimes require a small runtime patch. When quantization formats change we provide conversion tools in the bundle with tests so the migration is usually non-disruptive.
[08:51] Sofia Martinez: ok, let's drill into the artifact transfer. Marco, how do you prefer transfers to happen internally? USB handoff, removable media, or staging node with turnstile?
[08:59] Marco Ruiz: staging node with a one-way air gap is our preferred pattern — operator uploads to a DMZ staging box, then a physically separate transfer node imports to the hermetic environment. No removable media unless explicitly approved.
[09:12] Ethan Cole: that matches what we've implemented with other regulated customers. We can sign the artifact and give you a verification script for the staging node.
[09:20] Dr. Lena Zhou: can Redwood's signed packages be verified offline?
[09:23] Ethan Cole: yes, signature verification is offline. The verification script validates manifest, hashes and signatures using public keys.
[09:29] Priya Nair: do you maintain a CVE alerting stream that we can consume offline?
[09:34] Ethan Cole: we can provide a signed CVE bulletin in the artifact or a periodic signed vulnerability export that you fetch during your maintenance windows.
[09:43] Sofia Martinez: let's cover escalation and emergencies — if we have a critical fix outside the quarterly window can we push an emergency update?
[09:50] Ethan Cole: yes, emergency bundles can be produced with expedited signing; we'd coordinate with your change control for emergency patches.
[09:57] Marco Ruiz: any limitations on model size? Our large denoising model is ~55GB.
[10:03] Ethan Cole: that's fine; hermetic nodes handle multi-file weight sharding. For very large models we'll recommend STAGING on a node with enough scratch before switching production.
[10:15] Samir Patel: a practical ask — can you produce a sample bundle now with a tiny test model so we can validate our transfer process?
[10:21] Sofia Martinez: yes we can provide a sample signed bundle and verification instructions. Ethan will attach that to the follow-up.
[10:27] Ethan Cole: I'll prepare a tiny sample artifact and verification script.
[10:31] Dr. Lena Zhou: SLA costs — will emergency on-site be additional?
[10:35] Sofia Martinez: yes typically on-site emergency support is a billable add-on unless negotiated into the enterprise contract. We'll include options in the pricing doc.
[10:44] Marco Ruiz: are there any pre-reqs for our infra — OS versions, container runtime?
[10:49] Ethan Cole: we support RHEL and Ubuntu LTS, containerd or docker runtime; specifics will be in the footprint doc. We also surface kernel and driver versions for GPU support.
[10:57] Priya Nair: audit controls — do you expose immutable IDs for each artifact so we can tie them to a ticket in our change system?
[11:02] Ethan Cole: yes the manifest includes artifact id and release ticket reference. We can integrate with your ticketing system via a signed export.
[11:10] Samir Patel: curious, how do you handle model explainability or red-teaming in air-gapped setups?
[11:16] Ethan Cole: we provide evaluation harnesses you can run locally. For red-teaming we'd provide tooling and guidelines but the actual tests run locally and you can optionally share sanitized reports.
[11:26] Dr. Lena Zhou: one subtle detail — we have a supplier vetting process. Will Redwood provide SOC2 and ISO attestation for the build pipeline that produced the artifacts?
[11:36] Sofia Martinez: yes we can share relevant attestations and a limited build pipeline SBOM excerpt; for detailed pipeline access we'd need an NDA and a supplier audit engagement.
[11:45] Marco Ruiz: any recommendations on rack/Cooling for H100? Power is constrained in our imaging cabinets.
[11:50] Ethan Cole: H100s are high-power; if you have constrained cabinets we might recommend A40s with sharded models or use smaller model families. We'll include thermal/power specs in the footprint doc.
[12:01] Priya Nair: final compliance question — if auditors want to run queries against logs, what's the export format?
[12:07] Ethan Cole: signed JSONL exports with cryptographic signatures are available; we can produce a read-only export that contains metadata and redacted request traces (no PHI).
[12:15] Sofia Martinez: ok we're approaching the end — quick recap and next steps. Ethan, can you summarize technical deliverables?
[12:21] Ethan Cole: sure: 1) sample signed artifact + verification script; 2) hardware footprint doc with recommended GPU SKUs and power/thermal; 3) ops playbook covering install/rollback/smoke tests and snapshot recovery. I'll aim to get these out by next week.
[12:33] Sofia Martinez: I'll share pricing matrix and procurement/contracting steps. Also include the SOC2 and HSM excerpt.
[12:40] Marco Ruiz: we'll compile our maintenance window calendar and security contact list and send to Sofia.
[12:44] Priya Nair: I'll confirm regulatory scope and any additional attestations needed.
[12:48] Dr. Lena Zhou: timeline — if we like the artifacts, we want to schedule an on-site ops run in Jan week 2.
[12:55] Sofia Martinez: we'll tentatively set that and confirm after docs are shared. Anything else?
[12:59] Samir Patel: just one more — can you include recommended quantization profiles for our denoising model?
[13:05] Ethan Cole: yes we'll include quantization guidance and expected perf tradeoffs.
[13:09] Sofia Martinez: perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the docs and action items.
[13:14] Dr. Lena Zhou: thanks all.
[13:16] Meeting end.
